content.title: About
content.content: Cottage cheese is a fresh curd product obtained by coagulating milk and draining the whey. Fresh cheese NFS (non‑fermented fresh) is a soft cheese made from whole milk without the addition of enzymes, preserving a mild flavor and high protein content.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Cottage cheese is considered one of the oldest dairy foods, made already in ancient Egypt.
It is known by many names worldwide: in Russia – творог, in Poland – twaróg, in Greece – τυρί κρέμας.
NFS cheese is often used in desserts because it lacks the strong flavor of fermented cheeses.
Cottage cheese is rich in casein, a slowly digestible protein that supports muscle growth over time.
In some regions cottage cheese is served with honey and berries as a traditional breakfast.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Both cottage cheese and NFS cheese provide complete protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Rich in calcium
items.content: Calcium supports bone and tooth health and plays a role in muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat (in low‑fat versions)
items.content: Reduced‑fat cottage cheese contains little saturated fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Probiotic properties
items.content: Live cultures remaining in cottage cheese can promote a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: These dairy products contain vitamin B12, riboflavin, and niacin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: People allergic to casein or whey may experience reactions when consuming cottage cheese or fresh cheese.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some NFS cheeses can be salty; individuals with hypertension should monitor intake.

items.title: Lactose content
items.content: Cottage cheese contains lactose, so those with intolerance should choose lactose‑free options.

items.title: Bacterial contamination
items.content: Improper storage can lead to growth of pathogenic bacteria, causing foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cottage cheese can be eaten plain, mixed into smoothies, oatmeal, salads, or used in baking. Fresh NFS cheese is often sliced thin for sandwiches, used as a filling for dumplings, or incorporated into desserts such as cheesecake.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cottage cheese and NFS cheese in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C in an airtight container. They typically keep 5‑7 days after opening. Discard if an off‑odor or discoloration develops.
